Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing alignment request + migration checklist

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency profile and the KV cache behavior on long-context prompts. We're doing an internal vendor re-eval and CloudHarbor (our incumbent) has come back with a renewal offer that is materially lower than the list numbers we saw in your deck.

Before we move to an RFP award, procurement asked whether Redwood can provide an equivalent commercial package that gets us to parity on TCO for year one. Key items they care about:
- First 3 months protected pilot credits or runtime discounts
- A clear mapping of seat/throughput pricing vs our current machine-hour billing
- Any one-time migration assistance (credits or engineering hours)

Attached is the RFP summary and a high-level usage profile. Can we get a quick economic sketch and the constraints that would prevent a direct price-match? We're not asking you to beat the incumbent, just to show a pathway to equivalent unit economics so we can justify Redwood internally.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — procurement wants options by Friday.

Best,
Lila Banerjee
Head of Platform, EdgeQuest

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>

Hi Lila — thanks for sending this over and for the candid ask. Short answer: yes, we can put together a competitive package; I want to be transparent about the tradeoffs so we set proper expectations.

Quick sketch (high level):
- Pilot: $0 runtime for first 90 days capped to the first 5M generated tokens OR a $30k pilot credit — whichever is greater.
- Year-1 pricing: target ~15–20% unit discount relative to our listed hosted rates for committed throughput (baked into a 12-month consumption commitment).
- Migration assistance: 40 engineering hours of onboarding (remote) + accelerated priority support during cutover. Additional on-prem or VPC handoffs would be scoped separately.

Constraints to be aware of:
- Deep egress-heavy inference patterns (very long KV lifetimes, frequent full-context replays) materially increase GPU utilization; those would influence the final commit sizing and thus the discount available.
- If they require dedicated pool SLA (Reserved GPUs) vs hosted, the economics shift — dedicated carries capacity costs we account for in the commit.

I'll draft a formal commercial outline and loop in Marissa for approval on the concession sizing this afternoon. Can you confirm the 90-day pilot window is an acceptable shape?

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Fwd: EdgeQuest: pricing alignment request + migration checklist

Marissa / Jonas — forwarding EdgeQuest's RFP and my proposed sketch. Procurement expects a competitive alternative by Friday. Thoughts and approval request below.

Proposed package we can offer to hit near-term TCO parity: 
- 90-day pilot credit: $30k (applied against invoices) + priority onboarding (40h)
- 12-month committed consumption: $250k commit billed monthly with a 17% effective token discount vs list for the committed volume
- One-time migration uplift: discounted engineering add-on (extra 40h at 50% off) or a one-time $12k credit
- Operational guarantees: two-week SLA-freeze window during cutover and dedicated migration Slack channel

Rationale and risk notes:
- If EdgeQuest insists on Reserved/Dedicated GPU pools for year-1 we should reduce the percent concession to 12% because of capacity carry.
- Their usage profile shows intense long-context inference spikes — recommend we include a KV cache audit as part of onboarding to identify prefix hits we can cache (30–60% token reduction potential in some flows).

Approval asks:
1) Approve $30k pilot credit + $12k migration credit (or equivalent hours).
2) Approve up to 17% effective discount on a $250k 12-month commit (if they sign a hosted commit).
3) If they go Dedicated, authorize fallback concession to 12% or a negotiable seat-based uplift.

If approved I'll send a short-slide commercial summary and an SOW draft.

Thanks,
Steph

- Pilot shape: the 90-day window with a $30k credit is acceptable, but we need the 60-day checkpoint in writing.
- We prefer hosted first, Dedicated only if the pilot demonstrates consistent >70% sustained utilization.
- The incumbent is offering a 20% discount on list for year-1 plus $25k onboarding credit; to land the internal committee we need either a matching 20% or an equivalent blend of pilot + migration credits that sum to ~$45k in year-1 value.

Counter-proposal:
- Keep your $30k pilot credit + $12k migration credit = $42k total year-1 concession.
- Match at 18% effective discount on the $250k commit (subject to legal T&Cs).

If you can accept that, procurement will greenlight the commercial summary and route it to legal for a redline. Can you confirm by EOD tomorrow?

Best,
Lila
